He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford Cardinal]] and is a member of the [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canadian national team]]. ==High school career== Powell was born in [[Toronto, Ontario]] to a white Canadian father and Jamaican mother.{{Cite web|url=https://andscape.com/features/mavericks-dwight-powell-has-always-been-proud-of-who-he-is-and-where-hes-from/|title=Mavericks' Dwight Powell has always been proud of who he is and where he's from|first=Marc J.|last=Spears|date=May 26, 2022}} He then moved to the U.S. and attended [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]]. As a senior, he averaged 23.2 points, 11.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 2.3 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.gostanford.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30600&ATCLID=208169745|title=#33 Dwight Powell|work=GoStanford.com|access-date=June 26, 2014|archive-date=July 14, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714203842/http://www.gostanford.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30600&ATCLID=208169745|url-status=dead}} Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Powell was listed as the No. 8 power forward and the No. 25 player in the nation in 2010.{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/84429|title=Dwight Powell|work=Rivals.com|access-date=February 7, 2016}} ==College career== As a freshman at [[Stanford University]] in 2010–11, Powell earned Pac-10 All-Freshman Team honours. He started in 26 of 31 games, averaging 8.1 points and 5.2 rebounds per game. As a sophomore in 2011–12, the [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Cardinal]] won the NIT championship, and Powell earned Pac-12 All-Academic Honorable Mention selection. He started in 11 of 35 games, logging an average of 5.8 points and 4.6 rebounds per game. As a junior in 2012–13, Powell earned second-team NABC All-District, first-team All-Pac-12, and Pac-12 All-Academic second-team honours. He was also named the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Most Improved Player of The Year|Pac-12 Most Improved Player of the Year]]. Powell started in all 34 games, averaging 14.9 points to go with 8.4 rebounds per game. As a senior in 2013–14, Powell earned first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] honours for the second straight year and was named to the NCAA All-South Regional Team. He was also named the Pac-12 Scholar-Athlete of the Year and a Pac-12 All-Academic Honorable Mention selection. Powell started in all 36 games, putting up an average of 14.0 points and 6.9 rebounds per game. ==Professional career== ===Boston Celtics (2014)=== On June 26, 2014, Powell was selected with the 45th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|last=Steinberg|first=Russell|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2014/6/26/5848224/dwight-powell-charlotte-hornets-nba-draft-results-2014|title=2014 NBA Draft Results: Charlotte Hornets select Dwight Powell with 45th pick|work=SBNation.com|date=June 26, 2014|access-date=February 7, 2016}} On July 12, Powell's rights were traded, along with [[Brendan Haywood]], to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in exchange for [[Scotty Hopson]] and cash considerations.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/hopson-acquired-cavs|title=Hopson Acquired from Cavs|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 12, 2014|access-date=February 7, 2016}} He then joined the Cavaliers for the [[2014 NBA Summer League|NBA Summer League]] and signed with them on August 23.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/powell-signing-140823|title=Cavs Sign Dwight Powell|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=August 23, 2014|access-date=February 7, 2016}} On September 25, he was traded, along with [[John Lucas III]], [[Erik Murphy]], [[Malcolm Thomas (basketball, born 1988)|Malcolm Thomas]] and the Cavaliers' 2016 and 2017 second-round picks, to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for [[Keith Bogans]] and two future second-round picks.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-announce-roster-moves|title=Boston Celtics Announce Roster Moves|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=September 25, 2014|access-date=February 7, 2016}} During his time with the Celtics, he was assigned multiple times to the [[Maine Red Claws]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|publisher=National Basketball 2015, he scored a season-high 11 points on 5-for-7 shooting in a loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150114/DALDEN/gameinfo.html|title=Lawson, Faried lead Nuggets the [[Texas Legends]] during his rookie season. In July 2015, Powell joined the Mavericks for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]]. 2019}} On April 3, 2019, he scored 25 points in a 110–108 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071845|title=Towns, Wiggins help T-wolves turn 2019.{{Cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-dwight-powell-to-contract-extension/|title=Mavericks sign Dwight Powell to contract extension|website=mavs.com|date=July 6, 2019 |access-date=July 6, 2019}} On December 4, 2019, Powell set a season-high 24 points while recording five rebounds, four assists, one steal and two blocks in a 121–114 win against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. He had a perfect shooting night, going 9 of 9 from the field and 2 of 2 from the three-point line. Once the fourth quarter started, Powell experienced a left arm injury and got ruled out of the game.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/mavs-news-dwight-powell-ends-perfect-night-with-left-arm-injury-timberwolves-x-rays-negative/|title=Mavs news: Dwight Powell ends perfect shooting night with left arm injury vs. Timberwolves, X-rays negative|publisher=ClutchPoints.com|date=December 4, 2019|access-date=March 2, 2020}} On January 21, 2020, in a game against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], Powell suffered a season-ending [[Achilles tendon rupture|Achilles tendon]] injury while attempting to drive to the basket.Wright, Michael C. Achilles injury|date=January 28, 2020|publisher=ESPN|agency=Associated Press|access-date=January 26, 2021}} Powell was one of only 4 other players in the NBA to play all 82 games in a season in the [[2021–22 NBA season]], as well as breaking the Mavericks franchise record for most consecutive field goals made with 18 in a stretch of 4 games.{{Cite web |last=Trigg |first=Dalton |title=He Can't Miss!: Dwight Powell Breaks Mavs Record For Consecutive Shots Made |url=https://www.si.com/nba/mavericks/news/dwight-powell-breaks-dallas-mavs-record-luka-doncic-jason-kidd-san-antonio-spurs |access-date=April 13, 2022 |website=Sports Illustrated |date=April 10, 2022 |language=en}}{{Cite tweet |title=Dwight Powell made 18 consecutive field goals over the past 4 games, leading up to a miss web|url=https://www.mavs.com/powell-re-signs/|title=Mavericks re-sign franchise foundation piece Powell|website=mavs.com|date=July 9, 2023|access-date=July 10, 2023}} Powell reached the [[2024 NBA 2022, Powell agreed to a three-year commitment to play with the Canadian senior men's national team.{{Cite web |title=FOURTEEN ATHLETES COMMITTED TO REPRESENT CANADA AS SENIOR MEN'S NATIONAL TEAM He was named to Canada's roster for the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Summer Olympics in Paris]].{{cite web| title = Gilgeous-Alexander, Murray to lead NBA-experienced Canadian Olympic
